To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a three-dimensional optical cavity with a finesse of 2000 and an average power of 1.3 kW was constructed and that the cavity was operated with a laser spot size of 10 μ m at the interaction point.

we have successfully designed and demonstrated a high-finesse optical cavity with 4 mirrors for the laser–electron beam interaction, which is essential for the development of intense photon beams by laser-Comptonscattering.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of generating 2.7 billion 24 MeVs gamma rays per second using the 2.6 kW laser beam in the optical cavity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an intense photon source for the application of laser Compton scattering.
the development of a three-dimensional optical cavity for the laser–Compton source.
the development of an optical cavity for a laser-Compton source with a high power laser and a high current electron beam.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 4-mirror cavity has a great potential for the development of intense photon source with a laser-Compton process.
a 4-mirror cavity with the vertical beam spot size of about 10 μ m in σ is feasible for the generation of 10 10 photons/s in a wide energy range from 10 MeV up to 200 MeV.
we have successfully developed the 4-mirror cavity for the laser–Compton scattering experiment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a three-dimensional 3-mirror optical cavity and achieved a high finesse of 3000, average power of 1.8 kW and 2.2×10 9 photons/s.
we successfully developed a three dimensional optical cavity with the vertical spot size of 10 μ m in σ for the laser-Compton gamma-ray source.
we developed the first three-dimensional four-mirror optical cavity with a vertical beam size of 13 μ m, which is the most challenging condition to realize in this field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the three-dimensional 4 mirror optical cavity can be used to develop a compact, high-power, and high-energy photon source by laser-Comptom scattering.
the cavity with a vertical laser beam can be operated with a high finesse and a high power.
we have demonstrated the possibility of achieving the high power and high finesse optical cavity with the vertical beam configuration.
